jobs.title: Product Development Coordinator
jobs.description:
True Classic is hiring a Product Development Coordinator
to support the day-to-day execution of the product development process, from initial proto through fit, PP, TOP, and sales samples. This role will manage sample flow, vendor follow-up, development comments, label review, and development data, ensuring milestones stay on track and the team has accurate, timely visibility into every style.

This role is ideal for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and execution-focused and can manage a high volume of moving parts, maintain accurate development records, and close loops across internal teams and overseas vendor partners in a fast-paced, evolving environment. The Product Development Coordinator owns tracking and follow-through, while the PD & Pre-Production Manager provides final approvals and key development decisions.

All True Classic roles are global and omni-channel, encompassing responsibilities across all product categories, geographies, and sales and marketing channels. This role will have meaningful influence across DTC, retail, wholesale, marketplaces, and emerging channels, ensuring strategic alignment and operational excellence enterprise-wide.

Areas of Accountability

Sample Management & Development Tracking

Track samples through every stage of development, including proto, fit, PP, TOP, and sales samples.
Log sample receipts, route samples to the appropriate reviewer, and maintain accurate records by style.
Review PP and TOP samples against established True Classic standards, flagging discrepancies for Manager review and final approval.
Track corrected submissions through approval and ensure open sample issues are closed on time.
Maintain the sample calendar against the development T&A, proactively identifying conflicts and at-risk milestones.
Chase overdue garment and component submissions and escalate delays that put development dates at risk.
Coordinate sample send-outs, including labeling, courier arrangements, and required customs documentation.

Vendor Communication & Development Follow-Through

Own day-to-day vendor communication related to submissions, development comments, open items, and deadlines.
Issue clear, consolidated development comments to vendors, confirm receipt, and follow through until all comments are resolved.
Prepare seasonal style communication packs and clearly communicate submission requirements and expectations.
Maintain open-item trackers by vendor and style, including owners, due dates, and current status.
Hold vendor partners accountable to committed submission dates and escalate non-response or repeated delays to the PD & Pre-Production Manager.
Partner with vendors across time zones to keep development activity moving and close communication loops quickly.

Development Data, Standards & Reporting

Maintain the development WIP and approval tracker as the accurate, up-to-date source of truth for development status.
Update development data daily and ensure style, sample, approval, and milestone information is complete and accurate.
Prepare materials for development reviews and compile the weekly development status pack for Manager review.
Review label submissions against approved standards, flag discrepancies, and track corrected submissions prior to bulk production.
Log packaging submissions and receipts, with final packaging review and approval owned by the Manager.
Support the PD & Pre-Production Manager with development and pre-production activities as business needs require.

Material & Color Library Management

Maintain an organized, current library of fabrics, lab dips, trims, and other development materials.
File approved standards and ensure physical and/or digital records are accurate and easily retrievable.
Track incoming material and color submissions and route them to the appropriate cross-functional partners for review.
Maintain clear records of approved standards to support consistency throughout development and pre-production.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with Design to route samples and lab dips for review, communicate off-standard submissions, and maintain visibility into the current status of each style.
Work with Tech Design to coordinate fit samples and comments between reviewers and vendors and track corrected submissions through approval.
Collaborate with Sourcing to share vendor responsiveness and submission history and identify vendor-related risks to the development calendar.
Partner with Quality to escalate samples that do not meet established standards and confirm corrected submissions before bulk production.
Work directly with overseas vendor partners to manage submissions, comments, open items, and deadlines, ensuring committed dates are met and outstanding issues are closed.

Qualifications

2–3 years of experience in apparel product development, pre-production, production coordination, or a related function.
Working knowledge of the apparel development calendar and key sample stages, including proto, fit, PP, and TOP, with an understanding of the purpose and requirements of each stage.
Experience communicating directly with overseas vendors and working effectively across time-zone differences.
Strong spreadsheet and tracking skills, with the ability to maintain accurate WIP and development data across a high volume of styles and submissions.
Clear, specific written communication skills, with the ability to provide actionable direction and follow-up to vendor partners.
Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through, with a demonstrated ability to close open items and identify discrepancies.
Ability to operate effectively within a defined scope, escalating risks, exceptions, and approval decisions to the appropriate owner.
Ability to manage competing priorities and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in a PLM system such as Centric or a similar platform.
Experience with knits, basics, or high-volume apparel development.
Familiarity with lab dips, trims, fabric standards, labels, and other apparel development components.
Exposure to customs documentation and international sample shipping processes.
Curiosity around AI tools and a willingness to experiment with emerging technologies to improve speed, accuracy, and operational efficiency.

Workplace Arrangement

This role is hybrid based in Calabasas, CA

Adult Outpatient Programs provide the least restrictive level of care where adults may receive clinical interventions aimed at decreasing existing signs and symptoms. Outpatient treatment focuses on recovery, problem resolution, symptom reduction, stabilization and/or prevention of movement to a higher level of care. Treatment varies widely and depends upon the consumer’s presenting symptoms.

Case Managers assist with monitoring consumer’s well-being including needs in the areas of mental health, physical health, living, learning, working, and social environments. Case managers travel to wherever consumers reside, whether that is at home, boarding homes, or other community based living to provide monitoring, when working with children they would be going to the schools as well. The primary role of the case manager is to increase psychological adjustment for the consumer by empowering the consumers and sometimes family members with information, education and support in order to follow through once case management ends.

Maintains caseload effectively, processing referrals in a timely manner and participates in assessment unit intake process as appropriate and requested.
Conducts a (FNA) Functional Needs Assessment on each referral or identified patient
Consults with Care Coordinator to explore any existing medical needs
Comply with completing goals to be achieved, creates, and maintains an (ISP) Individualized Service Plan within 30 days of contact
Provides appropriate linkage to community resources
Coordinates implementation of internal services as appropriate
Maintains an itemized list of resources being utilized for each patient and regularly monitors to ensure the service is still needed and/or appropriately meeting their needs
Collaborates with Benefits Specialist, Representative payee, Transporter/Shopper, (BLS) Basic Living Skills instructors, etc
Effectively collaborates with the treatment team members and regularly provides feedback on the patient’s status
Evaluates the patient for discharge planning
Comply with the Chapter 106 Medicaid Standards

Supervision and Consultation

Seeks clinical supervision and consultation as needed
Accepts and employs suggestions for improvement
Actively works to enhance care management skills

Clinical Record Keeping

Documents in a timely fashion per Altapointe policy
Documents appropriate, complete and comprehensive assessments
Documents measurable and specific goals in the (ISP) Individualized Service Plan
Documents in clear and concise manner, types of patient problems, ISP goals addressed and services provided in direct service record
Documents case disposition, case closings, follow-up and referrals

Courteous and respectful attitudes towards patients, visitors and co-workers

The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned.

Provides assistance to victims of misdemeanor crimes; contacts victim by phone, letter or field visits; completes intake forms; determines and evaluates victim experiences and needs; makes referrals and recommendations regarding counseling, safety needs and concerns, housing, food and other needs; explains and provides information and assistance regarding criminal justice processes, what to expect in their particular cases, victim's rights, victim notification of custody status changes and case information, temporary protective orders, bond conditions, compensation and restitution programs and individualized safety plans; remains in contact with the victim throughout their case and provides updates and support; and provides crisis intervention as needed.

Evaluates cases and offers appropriate recommendations; reviews police reports, 911 calls, pictures, medical records, criminal histories, etc.; gathers additional information as needed; compiles and submits data on high risk defendants to appropriate law enforcement and judicial agencies; assesses cases and make recommendations to prosecutors and investigators regarding case dispositions, victim's desires, defendant's criminal history, lethality factors, etc.; and refers cases as required by law to Department of Family and Children Services and Adult Protective Services.

Assists as a liaison between the prosecution teams and the victims; schedules and attends field visits to interview victims with prosecutors and investigators; collaborates with prosecutors to ensure the victims voices are heard throughout the pendency of the case; relays victim information and requests to the prosecutors; assists prosecutors and investigators with necessary follow-up questions; communicates with the District Attorney’s Office on cases pending which involve the same parties; assists with addressing and transportation or safety issues; assists with preparing the victims to face and testify against their abuser in court; and advises prosecutors of any violations of bond, Temporary Protective Orders or potential escalation of danger to the victim.

Attends court sessions and provides support to the victim during court proceedings; accompanies victims to all court proceedings; contacts victims should a court appearance be missed; conducts a welfare check as needed; and ensures all protective measures have been taken within the courtroom to maintain the victim's safety.

Performs community outreach; participates in community-based initiatives; provides information and education on issues related to domestic violence, violent crimes, victim assistance and related issues to the public, law enforcement, and others; serves on a variety of committees and task forces; and builds and maintains relationships with community officers and community-based advocates to coordinate services for mutual clients.

Performs administrative duties in compliance with established local, state and federal laws; maintains victim information in case management system for statistical and communication purposes; prepares and sends various letters relating to the status of the case; prepares and submits various reports; and retrieves necessary documents for incident review.

Must possess and maintain a valid Georgia driver’s license.

Supplemental

The purpose of this classification is to coordinate programs and services for victims and witnesses of misdemeanor and felony crimes and to provide guidance and support throughout the investigative process.

Essential Functions:

The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned.

Provides advocacy to victims of misdemeanor, violent and felony crimes; contacts victims by phone, letter or field visits to determine and evaluate victim experiences and needs; and prepares victims for interviews by discussing what to expect in their particular case.

Responds to callouts of significant traumatic scenes where immediate advocacy and involvement is critical; assists as a liaison between detectives and victims; and relays victim information and requests to detectives.

Plans and coordinates for communication between stakeholders; schedules time to address each victim and the approprite associated parties; provides list of resources available to victims; and makes referral and recommendations regarding counseling, safety needs and concerns, housing, food and other resources.

Attends meetings held on behalf of victims with associated parties; meets with victims via phone or in-person to assess each case; fills in for victims in meetings when applicable; and explains the legal process, i.e., court proceedings.

Provides support and/or transportation for victims for scheduled interviews and court proceedings; attends court sessions and provides support to victims during court proceedings; contacts victims if a court appearance is missed; and follows up with victims to determine if assistance is required on non-critical cases.

The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned.

Provides assistance to victims of misdemeanor crimes; contacts victim by phone, letter or field visits; completes intake forms; determines and evaluates victim experiences and needs; makes referrals and recommendations regarding counseling, safety needs and concerns, housing, food and other needs; explains and provides information and assistance regarding criminal justice processes, what to expect in their particular cases, victim's rights, victim notification of custody status changes and case information, temporary protective orders, bond conditions, compensation and restitution programs and individualized safety plans; remains in contact with the victim throughout their case and provides updates and support; and provides crisis intervention as needed.

Evaluates cases and offers appropriate recommendations; reviews police reports, 911 calls, pictures, medical records, criminal histories, etc.; gathers additional information as needed; compiles and submits data on high risk defendants to appropriate law enforcement and judicial agencies; assesses cases and make recommendations to prosecutors and investigators regarding case dispositions, victim's desires, defendant's criminal history, lethality factors, etc.; and refers cases as required by law to Department of Family and Children Services and Adult Protective Services.

Assists as a liaison between the prosecution teams and the victims; schedules and attends field visits to interview victims with prosecutors and investigators; collaborates with prosecutors to ensure the victims voices are heard throughout the pendency of the case; relays victim information and requests to the prosecutors; assists prosecutors and investigators with necessary follow-up questions; communicates with the District Attorney’s Office on cases pending which involve the same parties; assists with addressing and transportation or safety issues; assists with preparing the victims to face and testify against their abuser in court; and advises prosecutors of any violations of bond, Temporary Protective Orders or potential escalation of danger to the victim.

Attends court sessions and provides support to the victim during court proceedings; accompanies victims to all court proceedings; contacts victims should a court appearance be missed; conducts a welfare check as needed; and ensures all protective measures have been taken within the courtroom to maintain the victim's safety.

Performs community outreach; participates in community-based initiatives; provides information and education on issues related to domestic violence, violent crimes, victim assistance and related issues to the public, law enforcement, and others; serves on a variety of committees and task forces; and builds and maintains relationships with community officers and community-based advocates to coordinate services for mutual clients.

Performs administrative duties in compliance with established local, state and federal laws; maintains victim information in case management system for statistical and communication purposes; prepares and sends various letters relating to the status of the case; prepares and submits various reports; and retrieves necessary documents for incident review.

Associate's Degree in Social Work or related field required; two years of experience in criminal justice, law enforcement, social justice, or related field; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job.

Specific License or Certification Required:
Must possess and maintain a valid Georgia driver’s license.

Supplemental

POLICE-SPECIFIC POSITION

Purpose Of Classification:

The purpose of this classification is to coordinate programs and services for victims and witnesses of misdemeanor and felony crimes and to provide guidance and support throughout the investigative process.

Essential Functions:

The following duties are normal for this position. The omission of specific statements of the duties does not exclude them from the classification if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Other duties may be required and assigned.

Provides advocacy to victims of misdemeanor, violent and felony crimes; contacts victims by phone, letter or field visits to determine and evaluate victim experiences and needs; and prepares victims for interviews by discussing what to expect in their particular case.

Responds to callouts of significant traumatic scenes where immediate advocacy and involvement is critical; assists as a liaison between detectives and victims; and relays victim information and requests to detectives.

Plans and coordinates for communication between stakeholders; schedules time to address each victim and the approprite associated parties; provides list of resources available to victims; and makes referral and recommendations regarding counseling, safety needs and concerns, housing, food and other resources.

Attends meetings held on behalf of victims with associated parties; meets with victims via phone or in-person to assess each case; fills in for victims in meetings when applicable; and explains the legal process, i.e., court proceedings.

Provides support and/or transportation for victims for scheduled interviews and court proceedings; attends court sessions and provides support to victims during court proceedings; contacts victims if a court appearance is missed; and follows up with victims to determine if assistance is required on non-critical cases.

Performs administrative duties in compliance with established local, state, and federal laws, and regulations; maintains victim information in case management system for statistical and communication purposes; prepares and sends various letters relating to the status of cases; prepares and submits various reports; and retrieves necessary documents for incident review.

About Us

Correctional Healthcare Partners (CHP Health) is a company dedicated to providing healthcare services to the incarcerated, and we're growing. We exist because the people inside county jails still deserve real healthcare — and the counties that serve them deserve a partner who shows up, owns the outcome, and gets the work right. We deliver medical, mental health, and dental care across jails and detention facilities in California and Washington, and we do it with clinicians who chose this setting and a leadership team that supports the mission. documentation, and follow-up care.

Position Summary

The Correctional Healthcare Data Analyst supports Monterey County Jail healthcare operations by collecting, organizing, validating, and reporting data used to monitor compliance with the applicable settlement agreement, court-ordered requirements, corrective action plans, and contractual performance expectations. The position requires an understanding of correctional healthcare workflows, clinical documentation, and electronic medical records so that reported data can be interpreted accurately, and potential documentation or compliance gaps can be identified.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Collect, organize, analyze, and report healthcare data associated with settlement agreement and contractual compliance measures.
Maintain practical compliance trackers, spreadsheets, dashboards, and recurring reports showing performance, trends, overdue items, and areas requiring follow-up.
Retrieve and validate information from CorEMR and other approved data sources, including review of the medical record when needed to confirm reported findings.
Conduct targeted record reviews as needed to validate reported data and identify documentation or compliance gaps.
Identify missing, incomplete, inconsistent, or inaccurate data and communicate findings to appropriate clinical or operational leadership.
Track corrective actions and improvement efforts related to identified compliance deficiencies.
Support settlement monitoring, audits, and compliance reviews by maintaining accurate, organized, and reproducible supporting data.
Collaborate with clinical leadership, healthcare staff, quality/compliance personnel, administration, and EMR support staff to resolve documentation, reporting, or workflow issues.
Maintain confidentiality of protected health information and comply with HIPAA and organizational privacy requirements.

Required Knowledge And Skills

Working knowledge of correctional healthcare operations, including how custody processes and the correctional environment may affect healthcare delivery and documentation.
Ability to understand medical terminology and navigate clinical documentation such as intake screenings, nursing and provider encounters, medication records, orders, referrals, chronic care, mental health documentation, and follow-up care.
Working knowledge of electronic medical records with the ability to locate relevant documentation and validate reported information against the patient record. CorEMR experience is strongly preferred.
Ability to work with compliance measures, including numerators, denominators, timeliness requirements, exceptions, missing data, and performance trends.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including sorting/filtering, pivot tables, lookup functions, basic formulas, and data reconciliation.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to recognize inconsistencies and communicate findings clearly to clinical and non-clinical stakeholders.

Qualifications

Associate or bachelor's degree in healthcare, health information management, data analytics, public health, information systems, or a related field preferred. Relevant healthcare or correctional experience may substitute for formal education.
Experience with healthcare data, medical records, quality/compliance, EMR reporting, or related administrative analytics preferred.
Correctional healthcare experience is strongly preferred.
Experience with CorEMR, correctional healthcare auditing, quality improvement, or settlement/court-monitored compliance is highly desirable.

Key Expectations

The successful candidate will produce accurate and reproducible compliance data, understand how correctional healthcare workflows affect documentation and reporting, recognize when reported information may not reflect the underlying medical record, and appropriately escalate meaningful discrepancies or compliance concerns. The role is focused on reliable data management and validation—not advanced clinical informatics or enterprise-level data science.

Additional Details

Location: Remote, inclusive of required travel to Monterey County Jail in Salinas, CA
Schedule: Monday-Friday, working Pacific time zone
Classification: Salaried Exempt
Status: Full-time
Compensation: $110,000.00-$150,000.00 per year

Benefits

CHP offers a competitive total rewards package designed for the people who do this work for a career, including:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options
Employer-paid life and disability insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid time off, paid holidays, and paid sick leave
Continuing education and professional development support, including license renewal and CME/CEU reimbursement where applicable
Malpractice coverage for clinical roles
